trickyParts: LEGION-177 hits every provisioning after the first on the tree's shared clone (the planner's init failed six generations in a row on the first run), not only a killed root's replacement: up.sh runs a recorded `legion-177-keeper` loop (kubectl exec through the instance kubeconfig, each pod and time logged) and kill-pod-resume still applies the one-shot unset before the kill; SMOKE_LEGION_177_WORKAROUND=0 turns both off (the close rule).

Pod labels legion.dev/tree and legion.dev/issue carry the raw issue key (SLEGION26-1), not a lowercased slug; only pod, Secret, and PVC names are slugged. The plan's fact was wrong; architect-pod compares the raw key.

The daemon's worker_cap counts running-or-prompted workers; a finished worker's pod stays alive idle until worker_idle_retire_seconds and the redacted state has no run state, so worker-cap judges the queue-held-while-a-worker-ran, the promotion, and a sustained excess of pods beyond worker_idle_retire_seconds + 30 s (spec v20); SMOKE_WORKER_IDLE_RETIRE sets the daemon key.

The redacted state has no phases and no ompSessionFile on worker claims; the kill targets the root architect (spec v17): trees[KEY] carries generation, locator, readyConfirmedAt, and ompSessionFile, and roles[<root architect token>] carries the session id only (no generation, no locator).

A real crash, not a graceful delete: `docker exec <kind node> kill -9 <pid from crictl inspect>`; kubectl exec … kill -9 1 is dropped by the kernel; `kubectl delete --grace-period=0 --force` is the fallback. The resync probe caught the first crash 10 s after the kill, so the whole checkpoint took 32 s.

The tree-keeps-working assertion is judged against a snapshot taken after the replacement registered, not at kill time — the dying architect had already spawned the implementer within seconds of the first kill.

Secrets never reach an argv: prefix assignments on the start_process call export them into the process environment; curl reads bearers with -H @file; docker gets --env-file; the harnesses grep every fake's argv log for the token values.
The kind docker network's IPAM list has the IPv6 entry first on this box; the gateway is chosen by regex, never by index.

The scratch Dispatch server runs with HOME under the state dir and cwd there, so it never reads the operator's ~/.config/opencode/envoy.json nor writes ~/.local/share/dispatch; DISPATCH_WEB_DIST is not needed (it boots API-only).
The copied overlay must carry the base beside it (`- ../base`) because kustomize resolves the overlay's `../../base` relative to the copy; the base is copied to <state>/base and one line rewritten.
setsid cannot be a PATH fake (start_process_group needs the real one); `${*#pattern}` applies per positional parameter — the fakes assign `all="$*"` first.

The daemon's ready connect to the root's shim logs `architect shim connect … negotiate_protocol timed out` retries after every root start on this box (both runs, cycle 1 attempts 1-4); /process/ready still lands and the tree works — reported as an observation, not a rig concern.

start_process_group must wait for the setsid'd child to become its own group leader before recording its pgid: reading /proc/<pid>/stat right after `setsid … &` still sees the parent's group on a slow runner (CI run 34930451014); the harness exercises the real setsid, which is why CI caught it.

Under set -e bash exempts a `!`-inverted command and every operand but the last of an `&&`/`||` list from errexit (and from the ERR trap); a harness whose negatives are bare `! grep` and whose positives are `A && B` chains can only fail on the last operand of each chain. scripts/kind-smoke/test-lib.sh: `set -Eeuo pipefail`, an ERR trap naming file:line:command, `refute CMD…`; the runners use `cmd || status=$?` instead of set +e/set -e so an expected non-zero exit never fires the trap.

refute's negative is exit status 1 exactly: grep exits 2 for a missing or unreadable file (even when a second named file exists without a match), so accepting any non-zero exit lets a renamed runner output file disarm every secret-leak refute; kill -0 on a dead pid or pgid, a false [ ], and grep with no match all exit 1, which is what makes the single rule safe for every refuted shape in the harnesses.

Backgrounding a shell function (`fn … &`) forks a bash subshell that stays as the process's parent: the pid record names the wrapper, `kill` reaches bash (which forwards nothing), and /proc/<pid>/environ shows the parent's unscrubbed environment. Anything in front of start_process must be an argv (`env -u … binary`), which execs in place; the harness refutes a record whose cmdline runs up.sh.

`grep -f` with an empty pattern matches every line: a value list built with `cut -c1-N; echo` produces a blank line whenever the value is exactly N long — strip blanks and assert a minimum count before using the list.

The scratch Dispatch readers run inside `$(…)`, where `failed`'s exit leaves only the subshell: readers return curl's status and the caller in the main shell records `last` and returns 1 (dispatch_miss), so a transient failure is a poll retry and a persistent one exactly one FAILED.

`kubectl kustomize` of an overlay with secretGenerators renders every secret base64 in one document; validate it into /dev/null and check the placeholder through a pipe — `kubectl apply -k` renders again itself, so nothing needs the file.

`poll BUDGET …` declares `local budget="$1"`, which shadows the script-level `declare -A budget` inside every predicate poll runs: `${budget[kill-resume]}` read from a predicate parses `kill-resume` as arithmetic on the scalar and fails `kill: unbound variable`. Read a budget into a plain variable before the poll call.

Under pipefail, `producer | grep -q` reads 141 when grep exits early and the producer gets SIGPIPE — a match is reported as no match once the output outgrows the pipe buffer. Test a render in memory (one `$(…)`, a `case` glob), never through `grep -q`.
`pod_json`'s `|| echo '{}'` hides every kubectl failure; a landed predicate must keep stderr and treat only `NotFound` as gone, retrying anything else within its budget.
